Title: How can we help?
Summary: First steps and common tasks.
Body:
Select a category or search for a topic. Help works offline inside File Compass.

Common tasks

  • Copy files
  • Open a network share
  • Extract an archive
  • Connect cloud storage
  • Change language or appearance

Context help

Press F1 in a dialog to open its topic. Back and Forward revisit topics; Home opens this page.

Title: Panels, tabs and selection
Summary: Source and destination panels, layout and selection.
Body:
Each panel shows its own folder. The active panel is the source of a transfer; the other panel usually supplies the destination.

  1. Open the source folder.
  2. Open the destination in the other panel.
  3. Select files and choose an operation.

Choose side-by-side, stacked or single-panel layout from View.

Linked browsing

Open two local or mounted network folders, then enable Commands → Linked panel browsing. Current folders become roots. Opening a subfolder mirrors the same relative path in the other panel. Missing counterparts leave the other panel unchanged and appear in the status bar. Leaving a captured root disables the link. No files are changed and no missing folders are created.

Title: Preview, viewer and editor
Summary: F3, F4 and Ctrl+Q.
Body:
F3 opens the viewer and F4 the editor.

Quick preview

Ctrl+Q toggles the preview in the opposite panel, or below the file list in single-panel mode. Available previews depend on file format.

Simple and batch image editing

Select one or more images, then open Commands → Renaming, metadata and images → Simple image editing. The same settings apply to every selected image. New _upraveno copies are created; originals and existing outputs are preserved.

Exact width × height forces both dimensions and can change the aspect ratio. Width only or Height only calculates the other side independently for each image after orientation and rotation, rounding to whole pixels. Explicit sizes may enlarge an image; longest-edge mode only reduces it. Percentage, rotation, format conversion and JPEG quality remain available. Metadata is not carried into edited copies.

Media converter

Open Media → Convert images or Convert audio. Add files, tick the desired entries, choose output settings and destination. Outputs use _converted; collisions get a number. Originals are preserved. Successful outputs are linked to transaction history and safe undo.

Images

Outputs: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF, BMP and GIF. Resize by longest edge, percentage, exact dimensions, width or height with aspect ratio. JPEG and BMP flatten transparency onto white. Multiple frames require GIF, WebP or TIFF, or explicitly select first frame only. GIF reduces the color palette. Metadata preservation depends on the output format.

Audio and audio from video

Outputs: MP3, AAC/M4A, AAC/ADTS, AC-3, E-AC-3, FLAC, WAV, Opus, Ogg Vorbis and ALAC/M4A. Choose bitrate, supported channels and sample rate. Advanced options include bit depth (16/24 bits; WAV also 32-bit float), audio track ordinal, normalization, and compatible stream copy. AAC and ALAC can preserve original video in MP4 without video encoding; unsupported video fails while preserving the original.

Stereo expansion requires explicit upmix. It does not recreate an original surround recording or Dolby Atmos. AC-3 and E-AC-3 support up to 5.1. Increasing bitrate or bit depth cannot recover lost detail. Outputs are verified before being committed. Cancel stops the current file and keeps completed outputs.

Rename and metadata · Transaction history

Concurrent conversions

Choose 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8 simultaneous files. The default is 2 and your choice is remembered. This applies to images and audio. Cancel stops all active conversions and preserves completed outputs. Higher concurrency uses more memory and CPU.

Converter settings, including destination and concurrency, are above the full-width file queue.

Bitrate and quality

MP3: CBR for a fixed rate, ABR for a target average, VBR for quality from 0 (highest) to 9. AAC and Vorbis: ABR target average or VBR quality, where higher values mean higher quality. Opus: CBR, VBR or constrained VBR, with a target bitrate for VBR/CVBR. Actual bitrate varies with content. Only applicable fields are enabled.

CSV table preview

F3 and Ctrl+Q display CSV, TSV, TAB and PSV as real columns. Automatic detection supports comma, semicolon, tab and pipe, including a sep= declaration. Quoted separators, escaped quotes and multiline fields are preserved.

Select a separator manually (including colon) or disable First row as headers in the toolbar. Drag column edges to resize; tooltips show full cell values. Disable formatted preview to see source text. Change text encoding in the top toolbar when needed.

Preview reads the start of the file (up to 128 KiB), with limits of 2,000 records, 128 columns and 100,000 cells. The status line reports limits; incomplete final records are omitted. Files remain unchanged.

Converter layout

Conversion settings contains the format and conversion parameters. Advanced contains optional controls without a nested scrollbar. Destination and parallel file count remain visible below both tabs. Switching tabs preserves the selected values.

The queue fits its columns to the window width. Long values use ellipses and full-text tooltips; status stays in the rightmost column.

Title: Copying files
Summary: F5, destination folder and transfer progress.
Body:
Copy selected files to another folder or connected storage.

Steps

  1. Select files or folders in the active panel.
  2. Open the destination in the other panel.
  3. Press F5 and check the destination path.
  4. Confirm and watch the transfer progress.
A file already exists? See conflicts and overwriting.

Copy or move?

Copy preserves the source. Use F6 to move files.

Undo and operation presets

Edit → Undo, or Ctrl+Z, opens this session’s file operation history (up to 20 groups, 5,000 steps per group). New local copies, created folders, renames and moves are supported. Copies are checked by file identity and SHA-256 before removal. Modified copies are preserved; original names must be free. Overwrites, deletions, archives and cloud operations are excluded. A group can be partially undone before an error; remaining steps stay in history.

The F5/F6 dialog can save, load and delete named presets for destination, include/exclude masks, verification, collision policy and flags. Loading does not start an operation or change copy into move. Review the destination before starting.

Locked files

Choose Which application is using this file? in a sharing error, or from Commands for a selected file. Windows Restart Manager lists available processes and can activate their windows. Save and close the file there, then Retry or Skip. Network locks may not be listed.

See shortcuts and linked browsing.

Curved arrow and transaction list

The curved Undo arrow follows the left/right arrows in the top toolbar. Green transactions are reversible, amber transactions partially reversible and grey ones unavailable, with an explanation. Select any available transaction. Partial batches explicitly offer Undo available steps only.

Deleting a renamed file disables its rename. For two successive renames, undo the later one first to re-enable its predecessor. File identity is checked; reusing a name does not inherit an Undo receipt. Overwrites remain unavailable even if new copies in the same batch can be removed. Availability refreshes and is checked again before applying. The journal persists, while safe Undo receipts are available for the current session only.

Title: When a destination file already exists
Summary: Overwriting, skipping and applying a choice to more files.
Body:
Compare source and destination before overwriting. Overwrite replaces the destination file.

  • Skip to preserve the destination.
  • Overwrite to replace it with the source.
  • Apply a choice to further conflicts only when the same decision is intended.

Title: Creating and extracting archives
Summary: Compression, destination folder, passwords and multipart archives.
Body:
Extract archive contents to a regular folder for further work.

  1. Select the archive and choose extraction.
  2. Check the destination.
  3. Keep every part of a multipart archive together.
  4. Enter a password when required.

Missing parts, an incorrect password or insufficient disk space can stop extraction.

Title: Network, NAS and remote connections
Summary: SMB, FTP, FTPS, SFTP and NFS.
Body:
Finding a computer does not mean it shares files. A reachable file service and access permissions are required.

Windows shares and NAS

Use a known SMB share path.

Other protocols

Configure host, port and authentication in a connection profile. NFS may require a system client.

Discovery can miss other subnets, VPN devices and nonstandard ports. Use a known address.

Title: Opening an SMB share
Summary: Direct UNC paths to a NAS or another computer.
Body:
1. Focus the panel address bar.
  2. Enter a UNC path such as \\server\share.
  3. Confirm and complete Windows sign-in if requested.
  4. Use regular file copying.

If access fails, test the same path in Windows Explorer and verify permissions.

Title: Connecting cloud storage
Summary: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and authorization.
Body:
1. Add an account in cloud account management.
  2. Complete provider sign-in and authorization in the browser.
  3. Open the connected storage in a panel.

Available folders depend on account permissions and provider limits.

iCloud Drive

Select iCloud Drive when adding an account. Enter your Apple Account and regular password in the wizard, then the code from an Apple device or type sms for SMS verification. App-specific passwords are not supported. Enable access to iCloud data on the web and approve access on a trusted device if requested. Disconnect and use Log in again when the session expires.

Title: Finding files and duplicates
Summary: Name and content searches and duplicate files.
Body:
Select the search root and set conditions. Limit name, mask and other filters as needed; content searches can take longer.

Duplicates

Review matching files and locations before deleting. Identical names alone do not prove identical content.

Large text and document content

Text is streamed without loading the entire file into memory. A size limit of 0 means unlimited plain text size. Select its encoding as needed. Results show a line or location and a match excerpt. Regular expressions operate per line with a bounded line length.

Enable PDF and DOCX content explicitly. Documents run in an isolated process: up to 64 MB per source, 15 seconds and 512 MB memory, plus decompressed XML limits for DOCX. No OCR is performed. Password-protected, damaged and over-limit documents appear in warnings. Content search supports local and mounted network paths.

Title: Comparing and synchronizing folders
Summary: Folder differences and transfer direction.
Body:
1. Verify the left and right paths.
  2. Review detected differences.
  3. Check transfer direction and planned deletions.
  4. Confirm only intended changes.

Title: Disk space analysis
Summary: Folder sizes, filters, exports and saved analyses.
Body:
1. Select the root folder.
  2. Start a scan and wait for completion.
  3. Explore results and apply filters.
  4. Export or save the analysis for later comparison.

Sizes are logical file lengths. Inaccessible entries are skipped; links and mount points are not followed.

Title: Language and appearance
Summary: Language changes without restart and theme settings.
Body:
Language

  1. Open Settings and select a language.
  2. Choose Save.
  3. The interface updates without restarting; panels, selections and transfers remain open.

Cancel retains the current language.

Appearance

Choose light, dark or system theme. Appearance previews while editing; Save persists it.

Command search and custom shortcuts

Ctrl+Shift+P opens command search. Type part of a name, select a command and press Enter. Settings → Custom keyboard shortcuts lets you assign gestures such as Ctrl+Shift+J. Release an occupied shortcut before assigning it elsewhere. An empty gesture disables the binding; Restore returns all defaults. Text input fields retain normal typing.

Title: Keyboard shortcuts
Summary: F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8 and Ctrl+Q.
Body:
• F1 — context help.
  • F3 — viewer.
  • F4 — editor.
  • F5 — copy.
  • F6 — move.
  • F7 — new folder.
  • F8 — delete.
  • Ctrl+Q — preview.

Title: Troubleshooting
Summary: Missing network devices, denied access and interrupted transfers.
Body:
A device is not listed

Try a direct share path or a connection profile. Check the subnet, VPN and firewall.

Access denied

Verify credentials and permissions on both source and destination.

Transfer stopped

Check free space, connectivity and the exact error.

Reporting a problem

Copy version and build information from About and include steps to reproduce the issue.

Title: Moving, renaming and creating folders
Summary: F6, Shift+F6 and F7.
Body:
F6 moves selected files. Verify source and destination.

Shift+F6 renames an item. Use batch rename for multiple names. F7 creates a folder.

Title: Deleting files and folders
Summary: F8, confirmation and permissions.
Body:
Select items and press F8. Check paths and the removal mode before confirmation.

Remote and cloud storage may behave differently from the local Recycle Bin. Check permissions and whether a file is in use when deletion fails.

Title: Properties, attributes and timestamps
Summary: Alt+Enter and changing attributes.
Body:
Alt+Enter shows properties. Change attributes edits supported attributes and timestamps.

  1. Select items.
  2. Set intended changes.
  3. Check whether changes should include folder contents.
  4. Confirm.

Title: Batch rename
Summary: Rules, numbering and name conflicts.
Body:
Ctrl+M opens batch rename for selected files.

  1. Select items.
  2. Set name, replacement or numbering rules.
  3. Review the name preview and conflicts.
  4. Confirm.

Image and audio metadata in both directions

Commands → Metadata from file names accepts patterns for names without extensions, such as [MP3.Artist] - [MP3.Track] - [MP3.Title] or [EXIF.Date]_[EXIF.Time] - [Image.Title]. Use literal delimiters; [Ignore] skips a segment. Dates use yyyy-MM-dd or yyyyMMdd, times HH-mm-ss or HHmmss.

Review old and new values first. Existing metadata is retained unless replacement is explicitly enabled. Only previewed fields are written and an exact .filecompass-metadata-….bak original is retained beside each modified file. Unsupported, changed or locked files get individual errors. Limits are 500 files per batch and 1 GB per file. JPEG, PNG and TIFF metadata is updated without converting image pixels.

Rename using metadata opens the collision-checked batch preview with a media preset. New fields include Image.Title, Image.Author, Image.Comment, Image.Copyright, EXIF.Make, EXIF.Model, MP3.Genre, MP3.Disc and MP3.Composer. MP3 tokens also apply to other supported audio containers. Missing values preserve the original name. See transaction Undo history.

File system dates and properties

Related actions are grouped under Commands → Renaming, metadata and images. Rename templates support [File.Created], [File.Modified] and [File.Accessed], with corresponding Time fields for the time of day.

Defaults are yyyy-MM-dd and HH-mm-ss. Custom formats use [File.Created:yyyyMMdd_HHmmss]. [File.Size] inserts file bytes; [File.Folder] inserts the parent folder name. File.* uses file system properties while EXIF.* uses photo metadata. These templates work for ordinary documents without changing timestamps. Sizes are not invented for directories. Creation, modification and access presets are available beside photo and audio presets.

See batch image dimensions.

Click the filename pattern field or press Alt+Down to open the available tokens. Choosing one inserts it at the caret or replaces the selected text. Writing metadata from filenames offers only writable fields and [Ignore].

Title: Disk health / SMART
Summary: Health, temperature, wear and diagnostic export.
Body:
Open Commands → Disk tools → Disk health / SMART.

  1. Select a physical disk.
  2. Read available data and authorize diagnostic elevation if necessary.
  3. Refresh, copy or export the results.

Support depends on the controller and USB bridge. SMART does not replace backups; a missing value does not prove a healthy disk.

Overview and export

Drive information appears on the left and SMART attributes on the right. Attributes split into two tables when needed. Narrow windows move the summary above the tables.

Prominent colored tiles show health and temperature. Save report offers PNG, PDF, TXT and JSON. Image and PDF exports include every attribute of the selected drive; long PDFs use multiple pages.

Select a disk

Click a disk tile at the top. Each tile shows health, temperature, drive letters and the model. Scroll the row or use the arrow keys when there are many disks. Refresh keeps the selected disk if it is still available.

Copy information

Copy information places the selected disk report on the clipboard. If another application keeps the clipboard busy, wait briefly and try again, or save the report as TXT.

Title: Checksums
Summary: Creating and verifying file checksums.
Body:
Choose checksum creation or verification from File. Checksums help detect changes to file content.

Keep checksum files with the data. If verification fails, check the selected files and the origin of the expected checksums.

Title: Favorites and workspaces
Summary: Frequently used paths and panel layouts.
Body:
Favorites make it easier to return to common locations. Workspaces restore a prepared arrangement.

Set folders and tabs before saving. Finish unsaved edits before restoring a workspace.

Title: Explorer, Command Prompt and PowerShell
Summary: Tools available in the Start menu.
Body:
Start offers Open in Explorer, Run Command Prompt and Run PowerShell for the current folder.

Virtual and remote locations may not provide a regular local working directory.

Title: SFTP and server host keys
Summary: First connection and changed SSH keys.
Body:
Configure host, port, account and authentication in the SFTP profile.

First connection

Compare the host key fingerprint with a trusted value from the server administrator.

A changed key

Verify the change with the administrator before approving it. It may reflect a reinstall or a different server.

Title: Panels, columns and previews
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
Panels, icons and previews

The Start menu contains Open in Explorer, Run Command Prompt and Run PowerShell, using the active local folder. The former External tools submenu and development-only project-folder shortcut are no longer shown.

Network combines Windows discovery, mapped drives, saved network connections and bounded IPv4 file-service probes on attached private networks. It checks SMB (445), FTP (21), SSH/SFTP (22), implicit FTPS (990) and NFS (2049), showing results progressively. SMB opens shared folders; newly found transfer services open their connection settings before connecting. A listening port indicates a possible service, not confirmed credentials or permissions. Large prefixes are bounded to the adapter's /24, with at most 1,024 candidate addresses and a time limit. Devices on other VPN subnets, IPv6-only devices, nonstandard ports or services hidden by a firewall may require a saved/manual connection. Permission-blocked probes produce a warning in the Network status tooltip.

Layout and navigation

The toolbar cycles side-by-side → stacked → single panel and shows the active layout. View → Panel layout also selects it. Ctrl+H switches dual-panel orientation; Ctrl+Shift+H switches single/last dual layout. Single-panel mode retains the active side; the other side keeps its folder, tabs and connection for later.

The toolbar groups navigation/selection separately from preview/edit/thumbnails. Hidden files toggles hidden/system visibility in both panels while retaining name filters. Invert selection and direction arrows follow it; arrows open the source folder in the other panel. Edit uses F4. Thumbnails change the list, not the preview.

Returning from a subfolder selects that subfolder in the parent. Automatic local refresh leaves the list enabled and applies only added/removed/changed rows, preserving unchanged row instances, marks and scroll position. Network watching is separately configurable and can be disabled for slow paths; Ctrl+R refreshes manually.

Single-panel mode has an adjustable folder tree with Windows names/icons: Home/Quick Access, Desktop, profile, registered cloud folders, This PC, Network and other available system roots such as Libraries, Recycle Bin or Linux. This PC includes local/mapped drives; Network lists computers and devices discovered by Windows, with cached and partial results available during discovery. Computers open their shared folders inside File Compass; other devices open through Explorer. Ctrl+R refreshes discovery. Redirected OneDrive paths come from Windows. Branches load asynchronously on expansion and can be retried. The tree tracks navigation and retains selection/expanded branches. Open an actual filesystem folder for file operations. Dual-panel modes hide the tree, even when older tabs/views requested it.

Unified preview

Preview, View → Preview, Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+Shift+Q control one feature. In dual-panel layouts it replaces the opposite panel; in single-panel mode it appears below the list. Changing layout moves the open preview appropriately and retains lower-preview height. Its header collapses/expands it, and the splitter changes height. Closing restores the opposite panel's previous contents. Hidden/collapsed previews do not continue loading files.

Images, text, syntax-highlighted code, Markdown, binary and hex views are available. Auto chooses the suitable view; Text explicitly displays source, with optional highlighting for supported languages. The formatting checkbox enables/disables code highlighting or rendered Markdown. Hex/Binary retain raw byte views. Find and encoding controls are available; text loads in bounded pages with offset navigation for larger files. Stable selection does not reload an unchanged preview after unrelated folder changes; modifying the selected file does refresh it.

Settings can use internal code/Markdown preview for F3. F4 uses the configured editor; unsupported types are not automatically executed through associations by F3. Settings → Save view and workspaces preserve layout, ratios, visible side, tree and preview state. Automatic view persistence follows its existing exit-saving setting; older settings retain compatible dual-panel defaults.

Rendered documents

Auto mode with formatting enabled supports:

  • PDF through WebView2, with pages, zoom and search.
  • DOCX through docx-preview, including text styles, tables and embedded images within library limits.
  • XLSX/XLS/XLSM/XLSB/ODS through SheetJS, with sheet selection and formatted values. Macros/formulas are not executed; charts and full original styling are unsupported.
  • Older DOC/other unsupported document formats through text extraction where available.

The ready state is shown after rendering. ZIP/RAR/7z in Auto show a read-only archive listing, up to 10,000 items with archive limits; manual Text/Binary/Hex modes remain available.

WebView2 Runtime is neither bundled nor automatically installed. When unavailable, rendering fails or the document exceeds 64 MB, a text/source fallback remains with an official Microsoft runtime link. Install separately and reopen the preview.

Workbook limits: 200 sheets, 2,000 rows and 100 columns per sheet. Compressed documents: 10,000 entries and 128 MB declared expanded size. Files are processed locally, read-only, without retaining a source lock after loading. The renderer permits only the selected file and bundled scripts, blocking unrelated network requests, new windows and downloads. Libraries are bundled, not fetched from a CDN. Licenses are in preview. WebView2 profile/cache uses %TEMP%/FileCompass/WebView2/<installation-id>.

HTML source and page preview

HTML/HTM/XHTML/SHTML in Auto provide Web page / Source code choices. Source is syntax highlighted without changing Office/PDF formatting preferences. Explicit Text mode also supports source highlighting.

Rendered HTML is static: scripts, remote requests, forms, navigation and downloads are blocked. Local CSS/images/fonts may load only from the file's directory or descendants, without traversing reparse links; auxiliary files are limited to 8 MB and unrelated file types are not exposed. If WebView2/rendering is unavailable, source code remains.

Archive/FTP/SFTP HTML previews prepare only the selected HTML file, not separate CSS/images. Code/Markdown views remain read-only.

Archive and remote previews

The same preview works inside an open archive and on FTP/FTPS/SFTP, including the cloud SFTP bridge. Archive files extract into a separate TEMP directory. Remote documents/images download a temporary copy; remote text continues to read a bounded prefix. Preparation shows loading before preview/metadata.

Selection changes/closing cancel preparation and remove temporary copies; source archives/files remain unchanged. Prepared copies are limited to 64 MB, with a 150 ms debounce before extraction/download. SCP uses F3. Encrypted entries require an available password; missing/incorrect passwords show a preview error.

File details and metadata columns

The expandable Details section provides type-dependent information and Copy details. In a lower single-panel image preview, expanded details move beside the image. General fields include name/type/size/creation/modification/attributes and tags.

Images include dimensions, megapixels, DPI, color/depth, transparency, frame count and color-profile presence. EXIF can include capture time, camera/lens, aperture/ISO/exposure/focal length, orientation, GPS, software and copyright; ICO/CUR include variants and dimensions.

PDF details include actual page count, version, stored properties, first-page dimensions and a text excerpt. Scanned pages without text need OCR, which this feature does not provide. Word formats expose properties, authors/editors, cached counts, paragraphs/comments, macro presence and excerpts. Excel formats expose sheets/visibility, saved ranges of the first six sheets, properties and shared-text samples; saved ranges need not equal nonempty cells. Presentation formats expose slide counts/properties/text samples. Office/ODF cached counts can be stale; formulas/macros are not run. Audio/video details depend on readable tags and available codecs.

Metadata columns load in the background; sorting by one also reads other supported files. Leaving the folder cancels work. Missing/unreadable values stay blank. Local/ordinary shared folders support these columns; archive/direct remote/aggregate/system listings do not scan them. PDF counts are read directly; Office/ODF counts are stored values.

Automatic and saved folder views

Settings → Appearance → Automatically adapt view to folder content is off by default. On entering another folder it inspects ordinary nonhidden/nonsystem files: a 60% majority of images selects thumbnails/image columns, documents select author/pages/sheets, music artist/album/title/duration, video duration/resolution. Empty/mixed folders retain the base view. Refreshing the same folder does not override a manually selected view. Disabling the feature restores the original panel view.

After adjusting columns, widths, sorting and display mode, right-click the header to save a view for this folder or this folder and descendants. Saved views apply when automatic views are enabled. More specific paths win; explicit saved views take priority over content inference. Remove saved folder view removes the current-path preset. Presets use config/folder-views.xml; the switch uses config/settings.xml.

Icon libraries

Action sets are Actions.Fluent.fvicons (Windows 11 color), Actions.Flat.fvicons and Actions.Outline.fvicons. FileCompass.Icons.dll contains seven app-icon variants with ten sizes from 16 to 256 px. Settings → Icons previews action/app choices immediately; Save persists them, Cancel restores saved choices. Changing the app icon updates application windows, not the embedded EXE icon or existing Windows shortcuts.

Create shortcut with selected icon writes a .lnk referencing the shared library. For the taskbar, unpin the old item and pin the new shortcut; Windows can cache old pinned icons. Keep the library/application at a stable path. Shortcut Properties → Change icon can browse FileCompass.Icons.dll; an EXE's fixed embedded icon cannot be changed this way.

File icons use Windows associations, including effective user registrations and registered icon resources, with recognizable fallbacks when needed. FVICONS are named-PNG data ZIPs, not executable assemblies. Icon DLLs are mapped as resources without executing code. Original app artwork is separate from third-party Fluent action icons; see libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-LICENSE.txt.

Title: Copying, recovery and operations
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# File operations and synchronization

Copy, move and delete

Use F5 Copy, F6 Move, F7 New folder and F8 Delete. Copy setup separates destination from file masks/options. Enter runs the default operation, Escape cancels. Choose an explicit collision policy rather than silently overwriting files. Optional controls include SHA-256 verification, timestamps, attributes, NTFS permissions, empty directories and hidden/system exclusions.

Local and network work can run in background queues. The active-job and waiting-job panels show actual work. Network details open when transfer starts. Background hides only the transfer window into the main activity area; click that area to reopen it. It does not minimize the entire application. Speed charts retain the measured history against operation completion. Network ETA uses real transferred bytes over active batch time, includes between-file delays, excludes pauses and waits for a measurement warmup. It remains an estimate.

Network queue lists are compact and scroll for additional items. Speed limits offer presets and a manually editable KiB/s value; 0 is unlimited. Local delete settings may default to the Recycle Bin; deletion still requires confirmation. Shift chooses permanent deletion. The Recycle Bin is unavailable on remote storage and inside archives.

Resume an interrupted network batch

Select the original source files/folders and the same destination, then choose Resume in copy setup. Verified owned partial files resume, missing targets transfer, and complete same-size targets are skipped. Different-size targets transfer again through staging. Already complete files are not fully hash-compared in this mode.

Ownership/checkpoints bind the server, account, source/destination paths, source size/time and sampled block hashes. Changed sources or invalid partial data are rejected. New uploads use .FileCompass-upload-…part; supported checkpoints from older versions remain readable.

A .part.fcinfo.xml sidecar describes original name, destination, length, modification time and transfer identifier. It contains no password or full local source path. This is descriptive only: safe resume also requires File Compass's verified local record in data/transfers. A filename or edited sidecar never authorizes adoption of another file. Successful completion removes the sidecar.

The network batch plan and completed-item receipts are saved during work. Interrupted normal network batches remain recoverable after restarting File Compass or Windows. Startup offers recovery; Commands → Operations → Restore saved tasks opens it manually. Sources/connections are revalidated, and only unfinished items continue. Successful plans are removed. Provider/protocol limits still apply: cloud uploads and non-seekable SCP work may restart the current file.

Folder synchronization

Open two folders, then Commands → Synchronize folders. One-way synchronization and explicit mirroring remain available. For bidirectional work select Bidirectional ↔ and Compare; content comparison is enabled by default but can be disabled for size/time comparison.

Review each row: →, ← or Skip. Bidirectional arrows correspond to the left/right panels. An unresolved ≠ conflict blocks execution; file/folder collisions can be skipped. One-sided items are proposed for copying; differing files propose the newer side, while equal timestamps require a decision.

Bidirectional mode does not propagate deletion or maintain a previous-run database. If both copies changed, proposals use current timestamps and remain editable. Both plan endpoints are validated before the first write; stale plans are rejected. FTP/SFTP use the shared transport layer.

Folder size overview

Alt+Shift+Enter or Commands → Analyze subfolder sizes calculates sizes in the background, with size/share bars. Press again to cancel/hide bars; leaving the folder cancels calculation. Local and mounted filesystems are supported. Logical lengths are measured, not allocated clusters or MFT records. Links are not followed. Skipped locations are counted in the status/tooltip and make totals partial.

Quick image processing

Select images and choose File → Quick image processing. Rotate 0/90/180/270 degrees; keep resolution, limit the longest side or scale by percentage. Longest-side limits never enlarge small images.

Outputs are PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF, with JPEG quality control. New copies receive an output suffix; originals and existing outputs are not overwritten. Name collisions are rejected before processing. EXIF orientation is applied before manual rotation. Metadata is not copied. JPEG/BMP replace transparency with white. Multiple frames are retained in TIFF; incompatible single-frame conversion is rejected. Cancellation can leave completed copies.

Move into an archive and split volumes

Alt+F5 supports Move into archive and split ZIP/7z volumes, including passwords. Move requires subfolders and a new output name. The archive is tested, extracted content is SHA-256 compared, empty folders are checked where paths are retained, and sources are revalidated before deletion. Files are locked, verified and deleted through the same handle; only empty directories are removed. A source change stops further deletion. Cancellation can leave some already verified sources removed, with their content retained in the archive.

Volume presets are 100 MB / 700 MB / 4 GB or custom sizes, using multiples of 1024. Outputs include data.7z.001/.002 and .parts.json; ZIP uses .zip.001, not .z01. Open the first volume with all parts together to browse, test or extract. In-place updates are not supported. Creation requires temporary space for a complete archive and never overwrites existing outputs.

Split and combine ordinary files

File → Split file creates .001, .002, … and a .parts.json manifest, retaining the source. File → Combine files finds the series from .001; with a manifest it verifies part counts, lengths and SHA-256 hashes, including the final result. Missing/damaged parts prevent publication.

Other programs' parts can be combined without a manifest, but original hashes and a missing final part cannot be verified. Retain the manifest for your own transfers. Input parts are never deleted; the result requires a new name.

Title: Search, metadata and tools
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Search, metadata and workflow tools

Search and batch rename

Commands → Find files, the magnifier or Alt+F7 supports semicolon-separated masks, regular expressions, selected items, recursion depth and size ranges. Double-click a result to open its location. Name/size search supports local/SMB/NFS, open archives and FTP/SFTP/SCP through an independent connection. Content search supports local/SMB/NFS files up to 64 MB, using BOM or UTF-8. Results are capped at 20,000.

File/Commands → Batch rename, the A/B icon or Ctrl+M supports local/SMB/NFS files/folders. Archives and direct remote panels support individual rename instead. Masks include [N] name, [E] extension, [C] counter, [N1-3] name substring, [E1] extension character, [RMD] modification date and [hms] time. Find/replace supports regex and case sensitivity. Numeric fields include increment/decrement arrows.

Live previews identify invalid names/collisions and block execution. Temporary names permit swaps. Errors/cancellation roll back in-progress changes; the latest successful batch can be undone.

EXIF/music masks can be combined with counters:

| Mask | Value |

| --- | --- |

| [EXIF.Date] | Capture date, yyyy-MM-dd |

| [EXIF.Time] | Capture time, HH-mm-ss |

| [EXIF.Camera] | Camera make/model |

| [MP3.Artist] | Artist |

| [MP3.Album] | Album |

| [MP3.Title] | Track title |

| [MP3.Track] | Track number, at least two digits |

| [MP3.Year] | Year |

Presets prepare photo/music naming schemes. Missing/unreadable metadata retains the original name and explains why; invalid Windows filename characters become underscores. Reading never changes file contents/tags.

Space marks a folder and calculates recursive size in the background, including archives and supported remote panels. Links are not followed. An error leaves <DIR> and reports the problem rather than presenting an incomplete total.

Metadata search

Alt+F7 → Metadata combines conditions with the General tab's location, masks and depth. Fields include width/height/megapixels, document pages, spreadsheet sheets, presentation slides, author/title/camera, artist/album/media duration/audio bitrate and capture date.

Numeric comparisons support greater/at least/equal/less/at most; text supports contains/equal/starts with. Case sensitivity is shared with normal search. Durations accept hh:mm:ss or d.hh:mm:ss; capture dates compare calendar dates. All conditions must match; missing values do not match.

Examples cover wide photos, PDFs over 20 pages, author names and videos over one hour. Presets change relevant masks/conditions while retaining other restrictions. Conditions persist in search profiles. Results show matched values and can be sent to a panel; the status shows the file being examined and Cancel stops work.

Metadata search supports local folders and ordinary network shares, not archive/direct FTP/SFTP search. Unsupported conditions are not silently ignored. Isolated workers impose time limits and skip unsupported extensions. Availability depends on formats/codecs and file protection/damage. PDF page counts are read directly; Office/ODF may report cached counts.

Duplicates and comparison

Commands → Find duplicates accepts semicolon-separated folders and scans subfolders. Files are grouped by size then compared using full SHA-256. Aliases/hard links to the same physical file count once; symbolic/reparse links are skipped and inaccessible items reported.

Results show groups, names, paths, sizes and a shared preview. Long path prefixes are shortened with full-path tooltips. Mark copies retains the first path in each group and marks the others; adjust manually. Recycle requires confirmation and rechecks content, size, timestamps and physical identity. Each group must retain an unmarked verified representative; changes invalidate the plan. Partial completion remains visible. Download/extract direct remote/archive content first; mounted folders are supported.

Commands → Compare by content / Ctrl+Shift+D accepts two selected files, one in each panel, or manually chosen paths. Text uses colored side-by-side line comparison with difference navigation and case/trailing-space options; binary mode compares bytes. Images use side-by-side or a slider overlay with shared scale/origin. Images decode to at most 4096 px on the long side; limits are 128 MB and 100 million source pixels. Sources remain unchanged; visual comparison does not replace byte comparison. Two duplicate results can use the same dialog through Ctrl-selection and Compare.

Code, Markdown and tags

Preview/Ctrl+Q/Ctrl+Shift+Q show source highlighting or rendered Markdown; the formatting checkbox switches to plain text. Highlighting works in Auto and explicit Text mode. Viewer settings can enable this internal preview for F3; F4 keeps the configured editor.

Markdown supports headings, lists, tables and code blocks. Embedded HTML is not executed, links are inactive and remote images are not downloaded. Text preview reads a bounded initial 128 KiB page.

File → Edit tags (also in the context menu) adds/replaces/removes tags. A quick filter such as #Important selects matching items; Commands → Files by tags also finds tagged files elsewhere. Tags live in the local profile and do not modify file content. File Compass moves/renames preserve tags; external moves are not automatically tracked. Where physical identity is available, a new file at the old path does not inherit old tags.

Workspaces, basket and recursive listings

Workspaces save named sets of tabs, sorting, views, split ratios and filters. They contain no passwords and do not reopen network connections without a user action.

The selection basket collects references from different folders. Delete/F8 removes basket references only; copy/rename/archive act on the referenced files. Recursive contents displays subfolder files with their locations; return using the parent item or Back to normal folder contents. Directory links are skipped; the limit is 100,000 items and inaccessible folders can stop loading with an error. Cancel via Escape/View. Basket/aggregate listings cannot be destination folders: open an ordinary directory first.

Everything and performance

Commands → Fast search with Everything uses a separately installed/running Everything index; only its SDK is bundled. Queries accept Everything syntax and return at most 20,000 results. The helper has a 15-second timeout. Ordinary Alt+F7 search remains available when Everything is unavailable.

Startup can use a JIT profile on later runs. Thumbnails load for realized rows and release images outside the visible area. Same-folder refresh applies incremental row changes and preserves selection/scroll. Performance depends on storage, antivirus and available caches.

Title: Archives and archivers
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Archives and optional archivers

File Compass browses archives as folders and uses the bundled 7-Zip engine for supported formats. ZIP, 7z, TAR/GZ and supported external RAR/ARJ/LHA creation are available according to the selected format/tool. Existing ARJ/LHA/TAR archives have read-only limitations. Archive operations enforce path, entry-count, memory, elapsed-time, expanded-size, free-space and nesting limits configurable in Settings → Archives. Passwords remain outside worker command-line arguments.

Compression progress shows the current file, operation completion and compression-ratio history. The chart's horizontal axis is operation completion (0–100%); the vertical axis is output/input percentage and can exceed 100%. The connected samples show how the ratio changes during the operation. See operations for verified move-to-archive and split ZIP/7z volumes.

Obtain optional tools

Settings → Archives can find an existing installation, select an EXE, or open Get add-on / Get WinRAR/RAR. Download begins only in the separate download window. Existing configured/common/PATH installations are used without downloading.

ARJ32 and LHa are prepared under plugins/archivers beside the program, without modifying Windows or Program Files. The window is modeless and supports cancellation. Completion saves the path; manually configured paths remain supported.

WinRAR uses RARLAB's original installer. After downloading, choose Run installer and complete its normal installation steps. File Compass does not run it automatically, install silently or redistribute a standalone Rar.exe. It subsequently searches for the installation; use Find WinRAR if installation is still running.

Sources and licenses

  • WinRAR/RAR 7.23 x64: https://www.rarlab.com/download.htm ; EULA https://www.rarlab.com/license.htm . Trial software, up to 40 days without buying a license. Downloading does not include a license.
  • ARJ32 3.31: https://arj32.com/ . Shareware under ARJ Software's supplied terms. The original ZIP/nested SFX are extracted only; SFX installation/test commands are not executed. Original license/documentation files are retained.
  • LHa 1.14i, GnuWin32: https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/lha.htm . The original distribution and documentation are retained. This is the LHa compressor, not the Lhasa extractor.

RAR/ARJ/LHA creation runs external processes without passwords in arguments. Legacy ARJ/LHA filename-encoding limitations still apply.

Integrity and maintenance

Downloads use certificate-validated HTTPS, a 128 MiB maximum and time limits. Pinned versions, URLs and SHA-256 package/EXE hashes are in ArchivePluginInstaller.cs. ARJ is verified before its nested SFX is opened; WinRAR installers also require Authenticode verification before publication and execution. Changed upstream content is rejected.

ARJ/LHA extraction uses the bundled verified codec in an isolated worker with normal archive/path limits. Prepared directories are published atomically; cancelled/failed downloads do not activate a tool. Managed archivers are verified and held open before execution. User-managed installations outside the add-on store use the chosen path.

There is no automatic search for the latest EXE or automatic update. A new managed release requires updated pinned metadata, license/package review and integration tests. A newer personal installation can be selected manually.

Title: Cloud storage and authorization
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Cloud storage: Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox

New Google sign-ins use File Compass's publisher desktop OAuth configuration, config/oauth/google.json. Each user signs in with their own account without entering Client ID/Secret. Without publisher configuration, new Google sign-in is unavailable with an explanation. Existing accounts retain their old authorization identity until explicitly signed in again.

Google registration status

As of 23 October 2026, the external OAuth app is in production but not verified, requesting https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive. Search Console website ownership is verified; Google branding verification still awaits propagation (Google requests a 24-hour wait before retrying). Restricted-scope review follows verified/published branding. An unverified-app warning and the 100-user project cap remain. Production status alone is not Google approval.

Website · Privacy Policy. Full Drive access enables management of existing folders, rather than only app-created files. Every user grants access separately and can revoke it. OneDrive/Dropbox do not use the Google client and are unaffected by Google's shared-client retirement.

Add an account

1. Open Connections → Manage connections → Cloud storage, or the Connections toolbar button and Cloud storage tab.

2. Choose Add account, the provider and a local display name.

3. Choose Sign in in browser; select your account, complete MFA and review permissions on the provider's page.

4. OneDrive may ask for a drive/library; work/school accounts may need administrator approval.

5. When authorization succeeds, choose Connect.

Multiple accounts per provider are supported. Provider passwords are entered only in the provider's browser page; authorization returns automatically. The app name may appear as rclone depending on provider/client; Google's File Compass branding is awaiting verification. Use Sign in again if authorization expires or is cancelled. Provider questions include explanatory wording and access to the original question.

Imported profiles

For accounts copied from another computer/Windows user, choose Sign in again. Authorization is independent of the original DPAPI key. A successful verified sign-in keeps the account name/identity and saves new local credentials; cancellation leaves the original profile unchanged. Other accounts/keys are unaffected.

The previous configuration remains in a protected .before-signin-… account backup. Remove account also removes these backups. Complete browser sign-in/MFA yourself.

Files

Cloud panels support browsing, Copy/F5, Move/F6, folders, rename and delete through the shared network queue; browsing can continue during transfers. Tabs/workspaces remember account identity without forcing startup sign-in.

Interrupted cloud uploads restart the current file; completed targets can be skipped. Editing/previews use temporary downloads and normal limits. Native Google documents can be exported on download where supported. Operations depend on service/account capabilities.

Cloud panels do not provide SSH terminals or direct metadata search. This version does not mount cloud storage as Explorer drive letters and requires neither WinFsp nor administrator installation for cloud access.

Disconnect, remove and revoke

Disconnect through Connections → Active connections or the connection-button context menu; saved authorization remains. Remove account deletes local configuration/tokens, not cloud files. Disconnect open panels and finish/remove pending transfers first. Revoke consent separately in Google/Microsoft/Dropbox account settings when required.

Local storage and protection

Accounts are in data/cloud; each has an encrypted rclone.conf and a key protected with Windows DPAPI for the current user. Copying the program does not transfer usable authorization to another user/computer. Cloud directories have restricted permissions. Tokens are not process arguments or user log output.

A hidden local helper provides SFTP on 127.0.0.1 only, with per-account passwords and pinned host keys. It is not accessible from the LAN and stops with File Compass.

Title: Third-party notices
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Third-party notices

Paths below refer to the installation root unless a source path is stated. Original upstream license/copyright texts are retained with each component; this English inventory does not replace them.

libcurl 8.22.0 and libssh2 1.11.1

Network operations use the native FileCompassNetwork.dll adapter in plugins/network. It statically links libcurl (curl/MIT-like license), libssh2 (BSD-3-Clause) and dependencies from the official curl 8.22.0_3 Windows x64 package. libcurl handles FTP/FTPS; libssh2 handles SFTP/SCP/SSH. LibreSSL 4.3.3 supplies cryptography. Dependencies include zlib-ng, zstd, Brotli, libpsl, the public suffix list, nghttp2, nghttp3 and ngtcp2.

Original notices are in plugins/network/licenses; BUILD-MANIFEST.txt lists exact components/source links and the plugin manifest records package provenance/hashes. Static libraries/headers/original downloads are build-time inputs under source/downloads/network; adapter sources/build scripts are in source/native. No separate runtime installation is required. FluentFTP, SSH.NET and WinSCP are no longer runtime components.

Sources: https://curl.se/windows/ and https://libssh2.org/.

External SSHFS support

WinFsp — Windows File System Proxy, Copyright (C) Bill Zissimopoulos: https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp (GPLv3 with FLOSS exception; commercial licensing https://winfsp.dev/com/).

SSHFS-Win: https://github.com/winfsp/sshfs-win ; component licenses/sources are listed in its License.txt/repository.

File Compass does not bundle these system components; it downloads unmodified official GitHub release installers only when requested.

7-Zip 26.04

Unmodified 7z.exe and 7z.dll are distributed in plugins/7zip without installation. Copyright (C) 1999–2026 Igor Pavlov. LGPL and additional terms are in plugins/7zip/License.txt. Corresponding sources: https://github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases/tag/26.04 and https://www.7-zip.org/download.html.

File Compass uses a separate command-line process and the bundled codec. WinRAR is not bundled; users select their own installation.

WPF UI 4.3.0

WPF UI / WPF UI Abstractions (lepo.co), MIT. The .NET Framework 4.7.2 libraries run under File Compass's .NET Framework 4.8 target. Microsoft dependencies: System.Memory 4.6.3, System.Buffers 4.6.1, System.Numerics.Vectors 4.6.1 and System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 6.1.2 (MIT).

Libraries are in libraries, original notices in libraries/licenses. libraries/manifest.json records versions, official NuGet URLs and SHA-256. CompactMenu.xaml adapts WPF UI MenuItem for compact menus and retains its copyright notice. Other controls use library templates.

Source: https://github.com/lepoco/wpfui/releases/tag/4.3.0.

SharpSevenZip

Managed wrapper: SharpSevenZip 2.0.128, LGPL-3.0-or-later.

Source: https://github.com/JeremyAnsel/SharpSevenZip/tree/f4c16a6a95ace333fa33f38c1d69e44d77812eee

Package: https://www.nuget.org/packages/SharpSevenZip/2.0.128

License and package metadata: libraries/licenses/SharpSevenZip.

The wrapper is distributed as a separate unmodified DLL; it uses the existing bundled native 7z.dll.

The pinned package and assembly hashes are in tools/fetch-archive-library.ps1 in the source distribution.

Microsoft Fluent UI System Icons

Copyright Microsoft Corporation. MIT license: libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-LICENSE.txt.

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-system-icons

Pinned revision: a347af95478f989038cccbf085978865264c048a (libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-SOURCE.json).

Original SVG and PNG sources are in source/ui/icons. Runtime action icons are bundled in icons/Actions.*.fvicons.

Color variants are preserved; regular command icons use blue, amber, green or red

according to their action. Asset import: tools/fetch-fluent-icons.cjs.

TagLibSharp 2.3.0

Media metadata reader, LGPL-2.1. Source: https://github.com/mono/taglib-sharp/tree/TaglibSharp-2.3.0.0 . License: libraries/licenses/TAGLIBSHARP-LICENSE.txt. NuGet package SHA-256: 3C3F5B55988F69E0BC84DC760FEB8351FEF4D5C09A322D88462E683D334DFBFC. The unmodified library remains a separate DLL and can be replaced.

AvalonEdit 6.3.1.120

MIT; source https://github.com/icsharpcode/AvalonEdit/tree/v6.3.1 . License libraries/licenses/AVALONEDIT-LICENSE.txt. NuGet package SHA-256 8AC3E5AA2BB6178D92CBE72C7900A683FAB0AEE66A8EAFA481611C444DBEE3E3.

Markdig 0.37.0

BSD-2-Clause; source https://github.com/xoofx/markdig/tree/0.37.0 . License libraries/licenses/MARKDIG-LICENSE.txt. NuGet package SHA-256 9CFA31D3A2EB694D3164F1A3FAB41A040C698A22E784CD4D76E50489D5698335.

Everything SDK

Copyright 2022 David Carpenter, MIT. Source and SDK https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/sdk/ . License plugins/everything/LICENSE.txt. Downloaded SDK archive SHA-256 F5716D9513CCE6B462B5170A0A2E7E081E191D9BCAC6774F5DECC061497DF443. The optional search feature requires a separately running Everything; this distribution contains only its SDK DLL. No indexing service is installed or started.

PdfPig 0.1.16 (Apache-2.0), https://github.com/UglyToad/PdfPig; Microsoft.Bcl.HashCode 6.0.0 (MIT). License texts and package metadata are in libraries/licenses/.

rclone 1.75.2 — cloud storage

Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox use official rclone for Windows x64.

Source/license: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/v1.75.2

Package: https://downloads.rclone.org/v1.75.2/rclone-v1.75.2-windows-amd64.zip

MIT license: plugins/cloud/LICENSE.txt; original documentation: README.txt. The executable hash is compiled into PluginHashes.cs and checked before execution. The package was checked against official SHA256SUMS; build-time downloads are under source/downloads/rclone.

Local document preview

  • docx-preview 0.3.7: MIT, https://github.com/VolodymyrBaydalka/docxjs; locally patched to render symbols and stylesheet contents without HTML parsing.
  • JSZip 3.10.1: MIT option, https://github.com/Stuk/jszip
  • SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3: Apache-2.0, https://cdn.sheetjs.com/; spreadsheets are rendered using text-only DOM cells.
  • Microsoft.Web.WebView2 SDK 1.0.4258.31: Microsoft license; the system runtime is not bundled.

Licenses are in preview. Documents render locally.

SMART

smartmontools 7.5 / smartctl.exe: GPLv2. License and corresponding source archive are in plugins/smart. The tool runs as a separate process.

Source: https://github.com/smartmontools/smartmontools/releases/tag/RELEASE_7_5
